errors.description: The model incorrectly assumed the presence of purple faces on the cubes without any visual evidence from the video. The Scene Description and Ground Truth explicitly state that no purple faces appear on any cube — visible or hidden. The model hallucinated purple faces based on the color legend, falsely inferring that every color must be present on each cube. This is a speculative inference not grounded in observed visual data.

errors.evidence_quote: Since none of the cubes have a purple face visible, all the purple faces are hidden from the camera.
errors.description: The model built its entire reasoning on the false premise that purple faces must exist on the cubes simply because purple was listed in the color legend. It then incorrectly concluded that since purple faces were not visible, they must be hidden — ignoring the actual fact that no purple faces were assigned to any cube at all. This reflects a fundamental misunderstanding of the task: the legend was for reference, not a guarantee of presence.

errors.evidence_quote: Therefore, the number of purple faces currently hidden from the camera is 6.
errors.description: Based on its hallucinated premise, the model incorrectly counted 6 hidden purple faces — one per cube face, assuming each cube must have a purple face. analysis_result.analysis: The model fundamentally failed by hallucinating purple faces on the cubes, likely due to over-relying on the color legend as a requirement rather than a reference. This led to a cascade of errors: a wrong premise (purple faces must exist), speculative inference (they’re hidden because not visible), and incorrect counting (6 hidden faces). The model ignored the actual visual configuration of the cubes, which contained no purple faces at all. This is a severe failure in perceptual grounding and task interpretation.
